MOBS
The Mobs in this Neighborhood have a predilection
for inflicting Poison and Sepsis Debuffs either through
their own attacks or the traps they employ. As such,
they also have incredible resistance to both.
Gobblin’ Gators
These are not true alligators. They’re clearly made
up by some alien writer or an AI that saw an alligator
and thought they were fun but recognized they were
too strong for this early floor. While their bodies are
proportionally too small, their mouths are every bit as
large as a normal alligators, if perhaps a little narrower.
They strike lightning-fast near the water’s edge
anywhere in the Neighborhood, but on land, their
stubby legs and oversized mouths make them much
more ungainly. However, even a single bite from one
of these creatures can be fatal, as their lack of dental
hygiene means they might well poison or infect a
crawler with Sepsis. They primarily lurk in the Still
Waters quarter of the Bogbricks Neighborhood.
Gnawtria
These amphibious mammals have both an insatiable
hunger for meat and all the equipment necessary
to take a huge chunk out of anyone they can find.
Gnawtria are large, about the size of the average dog,
and possess a very long, prehensile tail. They’re not
much for strategy, and fortunately for crawlers, they
don’t typically operate in groups.
Unfortunately for crawlers, they don’t need much
beyond their quick reflexes and their armor-piercing
teeth. (That is not a metaphor. Their teeth go through
armor as if it weren’t there.) Bitten crawlers have a
chance of becoming poisoned. The Gnawtria can be
found in the Vibrant Walls quarter of the Bogbricks
Neighborhood.
Gnawtria, Level 3
Have you ever seen a possum mixed with a beaver
and given blood-red teeth the size of small knives?
You haven’t? Well, you’re in luck, because one is
coming right for you!
These furry little bastards are aggressive, vicious,
and those teeth aren’t just for show. Their slavering
teeth phase through anything that’s not made of
flesh. If you value your ankles, start moving now.
Gobblin’ Gator, Level 2
These creatures are about half the size of a normal
alligator with twice the attitude. Although, if you asked
them, they’d tell you it’s not the size of the gator in the
fight, it’s the size of the bite from the gator!
These adorable little swamp kittens may have smaller
bodies, but their massive maws are just as threatening
and impressive as those belonging to their earthen
inspirations. Be careful near sources of water, or you may
find yourself shorter by a foot… or possibly a whole leg.

Bob Bilberson: Just Another Guy
Crawlers are encouraged to keep moving forward to
survive the World Dungeon. Many crawlers take a deal
upon reaching the Tenth Floor or lower, and Bob was
all too happy to get out when the time came. But then
something unusual happened: the right people sort of
just… forgot about him. He’s been in the dungeon ever
since, popping up in different seasons as an NPC with
no meaningful work, no job, no specific reason for being
wherever he ends up. But that all suits Bob just fine.
In his old life, and later in the dungeon, Bob was
frustrated by the intense pace of the world. But now, here
in Arcadia, he finds himself perfectly content living among
the Sprites. Their repetitive speech, the predictable days,
the guaranteed income from selling potions to travelers
who don’t engage in a lot of small talk—all of these make
Bob feel right at home. If he meets fellow crawlers, he
breaks character and helps them as best he can, but
afterward, he goes right back to the stress-free and
predictable life he always hoped for.
What’s the old frog-wizard’s weakness? It’s not some
special blade or the tears of an ancient fairy princess;
it’s that Grimblegore tends to be a bit repetitive in his
attacks. Once Grimblegore slips into a pattern, it’s
hard for him to break it. It causes him great distress to
change his plan mid-stride.
His preferred method of attack is “Fireball-Fireball-
Jump Smash-Jump Smash-Gloat-Gloat.” While he can
alter this plan on the fly if motivated, he really doesn’t
want to. Clever crawlers can use this pattern to their
advantage by anticipating his next moves and working
on not being where he intends to strike.
Bob Bilberson—Human Peasant, Level 50
Seriously, we don’t know much about this guy other
than it looks like he’s always been here. He just
sticks to the background and does his own thing.
He’s really helpful, and for some reason, none of the
other Mobs in the dungeon ever mess with him, so if
you need a helping hand, look for old Bill. Or was it
Bob? I can’t really remember.
Dread Wizard Grimblegore, the Lord of the Grimes.
Level 10 Neighborhood Boss!
Prepare for a cutscene like you wouldn’t believe—
it’s time for the crawlers to take on the big guy!
Dread Wizard Grimblegore is the self-appointed overlord
of Arcadia, and as far as you and me are concerned,
he’s got the firepower to prove it. His interests include
going for long hops on the beach, enjoying a lovely
soak in swamps, and raising the dead to eviscerate his
enemies—pretty standard for an amphibian-themed
wizard. Can the crawlers make this evil mage croak
for good, or will their skulls join the many adventurers,
knights, and plumbers that came before them?

Slimy Croakers
Within the Giant Spiders’ lairs live anthropomorphic
frogs wearing clothes made from finely woven spider
silk. The Slimy Croakers are the guardians of the Giant
Spiders’ lairs, serving as gardeners, cleaners, and
protectors of their nests, for which they are in turn
protected from the Vine Creepers, Literal Murder
Hornets, and Bad Llamas.
Slimy Croakers are intelligent and know they have a
good deal going. Their skin secretes a gooey slime that
can cause paralysis to unlucky crawlers. The “croaker”
part of their name comes from the extremely loud
croak they emit when in distress. It can be heard up to
a mile away and summons Giant Spiders to their aid.
Literal Murder Hornets
Enormous arachnids and camelids aren’t the only
things lurking among the plants and webs of this floor;
a sinister flying insect stalks between the buildings
and trees looking for prey. Their name isn’t just a cute
warning —Literal Murder Hornets are the assassins of
the insect world, sometimes taking jobs from others to
eliminate their targets.
Capable of shooting stingers out of their forelegs,
Literal Murder Hornets will not stop until the job is
done. Their love of their craft is so great that they even
attack crawlers without a contract to get much-needed
target practice.
Slimy Croakers, Level 3
Mobs keeping other Mobs as pets? It’s not just some
GM’s twisted power fantasy—turns out it’s true and
at least vaguely canon! While the Giant Spiders are
out hunting, making websites, or doing other spider-
stuff, these little amphibious guys keep their homes
clean and free of pests.
They’re adorable, but be careful of their slimy skin.
A guy touched one once, and his arm went numb for
an hour, and that smell clung to him no matter what
he did. I know what you’re thinking, and unless you
want to talk funny, keep that tongue in your mouth.

creepy smile on its face. It was metal AF.
If one of these wretched things gets on your tail, it’ll

ENVIRONMENT
To alien eyes, this Neighborhood is a textbook example
of the classic dungeon, including corridors that look
identical but lead to radically different dangers, choke
points disguised as conveniences, and sprawling
chambers designed to funnel prey toward predators.
The ADHypermarket boasts long corridors broken
by towering shelves that create blind corners and
ambush zones with the occasional opening to various
storefronts or mall kiosks. To an alien architect, this
is indistinguishable from a supply hall packed with
unstable barricades and loot crates, except that every
surface screams artificial cheer. Fluorescent lights hum
overhead. Endcaps promise joy. Nothing here was built
to be defensible, yet everything is, by accident.
At the Neighborhood’s swollen heart sits The Last
Food Court Standing, which can function as a grand
arena masquerading as a communal space. Open
sightlines, slippery terrain, centralized hazards, and
layered vertical threats make it a traditional kill zone.
Non-earthlings notice the brilliance of disguising an
execution pit as a place of rest and nourishment,
where prey willingly lowers its guard.
Threading between the ADHypermarket and the
Commons, in an uncanny approximation of a town
square, playgrounds and rest areas offer false safety
while providing cover, elevation, and noise-dampening
chaos. It is here that factions collide, alliances form,
and violence erupts beneath simulated sunlight,
reminding crawlers of normalcy just long enough to
weaponize it against them.

Canis Knights
Canis Knights serve as one of the primary guard
Mobs for Arcadia. Created by designers with a limited
understanding of how the monsters in old Earth video
games work, these dog-like soldiers wearing fantasy
armor are assigned to guard specific areas and march
in formation until they detect a threat. Once they
sense someone is invading their space, they attack with
ferocity until their foe is defeated or leaves their area.
While it might seem like they’re easy to avoid, the
sheer abundance of Canis Knights spread throughout
Arcadia (and occasionally on other floors) gives
them a distinct advantage. Rumor has it that a clever
crawler once defeated a battalion of Canis Knights by
somehow finding their closely guarded Shift Schedule
and rewriting it so they only guarded a lone tree in the
middle of a field. Since then, they keep their sacred
texts—I mean, Shift Schedules—a closely guarded secret.
Strict Adherence—Canis Knights always do precisely as
directed, doing little or no thinking on their own. If given a
certain schedule or patrol route to follow, they will do so
to the letter without deviation. This adherence to direc-
tives leads them open to those who would exploit their
established patterns and ways of doing things.
Grimes
Grimes were a tutorial creature that could be produced as
quickly and cheaply as possible. To help create more Mobs
more efficiently, they were given a self-replication feature
so that new crawlers could test out a variety of combat
moves on them without straining the system. Sadly, the
Grimes were abandoned in the testing phase, never to be
seen again—until Destiny took matters into her own hands.
That’s right—a wily, wayward Grime nicknamed
“Destiny” managed to escape containment, and before
she could be recovered, she slipped into the sewers
where she proliferated just like she’d been engineered to
do. But something in their shallow genetic pool slipped,
and now they just don’t replicate like they used to.
Canis Knight, Level 5
I’m not gonna lie, these things seem like they’d be
cute! Fluffy fur, pint-sized armor—you’d think they’d
be your best friend… until they move in to attack.
Don’t let their cartoonish appearance fool you; those
spears and swords are plenty sharp, and they fight
like trained warriors.
Still… it’s weird how they’re only able to walk
the same path over and over again, like they’re
machines. If you ever want a laugh, memorize how
they walk around the area and stay in their blind spot
until you strike! I mean, I think it’s funny walking
directly behind them.
Grimes, Level 5
Just when you think I’d run out of things to hate, here
come the Grimes! Have you ever wondered what it
would be like to stick your hand in a jellyfish? Well, now
you can, as these stinging buggers hide in cracks and
crevices before oozing out to strike. Just when you think
you’ve killed one, it splits in two! How’s that even fair?
You’d better be up on your game if you’re gonna kill
these things before they get out of hand. Here’s a
hint: don’t go into this battle blind. Visualize a plan
and see it through.

ENVIRONMENT
Arcadia is a land of brightly colored buildings, loud
music, and predictable yet comforting patterns.
Created from the suburbs of contemporary Scotland,
Japan, and New York, Arcadia would’ve been an
impressive feat of engineering for the World Dungeon,
provided Borant had enough time to actually finish it.
Peasant villages with straw roofs stand next to old
brownstone homes that were hastily reassembled.
Real clouds float past artificial ones with smiley faces
printed on their sides. It all shows that Arcadia was
planned, but the vision was poorly executed when
Borant had to rush the plans. Strangely, this made
Arcadia a charming place where fans with a taste for
old-school games can watch crawlers reenact events
from the electronic media of Earth’s past.
Three types of terrain exist in Arcadia: towns,
dungeons, and fields. The towns tend to look the same
except for a subtle change in color pattern. In the
dungeons, gray stone walls meet burning sconces and
skeletons set into the floor, creating a cold, imposing
atmosphere.
Finally, in the fields, Mobs gather in great numbers
as treasure chests sit out in the open under the
watchful eye of their guardians. The weather is never
constant in Arcadia and seems to change from field
to field. One field may be sunny and warm while
the field right next to it is cold and rainy. In fields,
changing the weather is as easy as taking a step or
two to the left.
But what really makes Arcadia stand out is that
it looks half-finished. It’s clear the designers were
going for a specific look, and several buildings in this

install turrets and moats, but large sections of Arcadia
still look like crumbled, abandoned homes.

These story arcs combine what you find in the
Webbinghoods into easy-to-assemble adventures; just

The sound of a gavel rings out as the crawlers come

Slimy Croaker has a speech impediment that lets him

innocent Slimy Croaker from being framed for
a crime he didn’t commit. The Slimy Croaker in
question? The notorious Ribboff, who promises
the crawlers some of his best treasures and a map
showing the lair of Neighborhood Boss Aranaea
Magnus —the Great Spider herself.
•
The sound of heavy rock music fills the air as the shouts
of “No Fear! No Fear! No Fear!” reverberate off the
ruined homes around the crawlers. Running at full
speed through the Webbinghoods is wily NPC Crawler
Zach Nophobia, and he’s recording a speed-run of
himself trying to bash as many spider eggs as possible.
Zach is utterly fearless, but also extremely reckless, and
though he invites the other crawlers to join him, his
antics start to rile up all the Mobs in the vicinity.
•
The smells of barbecue fill the air as the crawlers
come across a massive wedding party of Bad
Llamas celebrating peace between two rival
families. These Bad Llamas offer the crawlers food
and a trailer to stay in for as long as the crawlers
partake in the festivities.
All goes well until one of the Llama guests keels
over from drinking poisoned punch. The crawlers
must figure out who the murderer is and keep the
peace between two rival clans of Bad Llamas before
both sides decide to blame the crawlers instead.
•
The crawlers move into a flooded area of the
Webbinghoods, forcing them to climb high and
move along rooftops to escape. What they don’t
realize is that Vine Creepers have buried their
pods deep inside the buildings, and the crawlers’
footsteps woke them up. The crawlers must keep
moving to dodge the hungry plant creatures’
attacks while also avoiding falling into the webbing
stretched between the buildings.

The Mobs found in the Webbinghoods lurk among the
ruined houses and trailer parks, between thick stalks of
plants and enormous spiderwebs.
Vine Creeper
While the Giant Spiders’ imposing webbing network
and the rowdy trailer parks of the Bad Llamas
come to mind when most crawlers think about the
Webbinghoods, another sinister force threatens to
claim the unwary. Giant ferns, trees, and flowers grow
among the ruins, and scattered among these are
gigantic leafy pods in the shape of huge eggplants.
These pods wield vines that stretch for dozens of feet
in every direction. If these vines are disturbed, a Vine
Creeper bursts forth, ready to kill. The Vine Creepers
exist solely to capture prey and haul it back to their
pods to be devoured.

Audrey II breaks out of its flowerpot and shoots a bunch
of singing vines in every direction while trying to eat Rick
Moranis? Take away the singing and Audrey II’s huge
head and replace it with a giant transforming eggplant,

them to hunt. Vaguely humanoid (but rarely seen

shamble along on all fours until they descend upon
their victims in a fury of fangs, talons, and strangling
vines. Once they overcome their victims, the Vine

air, slowly opening and closing their eyelids as they go.
They lurk in the shadows above, where the lights of the

the literal definition of the “Evil Eye.” Those caught
in their paralyzing gaze soon have great difficulty

want to “see” what happens then.
ENVIRONMENT
The Prickly Pack Alleys are a classic Tutorial Floor
Neighborhood. Most of the area looks like an ancient
Earth dungeon that would fit in almost any video game,
with one exception: while the area appears to be made
of uniform bricks and stone, all of these are carved
from a rock that glitters bluish-green. Speckles within
the rock shine in the flickering light of the torches that
punctuate the walls.
Very few “main” hallways track through this part of
the dungeon, but each hall is at least large enough to
drive a full-size car through with plenty of room. At first
glance, these wide thoroughfares seem straight, but
a slight curve creates subtle twists and turns, making
navigation difficult.
The smaller alleyways, no more than six feet wide, run
alongside these larger paths. They twist and turn in a
labyrinth, sometimes running for miles before spitting the
crawlers out less than ten feet from where they started.
They can avoid this happening more than once with an
Unopposed Tracking Skill Check. Otherwise, crawlers
can pay special attention to either their minimaps or
maps they create and slowly learn how to navigate these
alleys to save time, but beware: the cramped nature of
these alleys makes them ideal for ambushes.

soldiers to their MisChief. They’re tough, strong, and

At first, you may have made the mistake of
thinking this was your garden-variety floating tuft
of fire. Given that it’s zooming directly at your
face now, you’ve likely realized you were wrong.

Sheol to serve as a foot-soldier. They’re bound to
serve their summoner’s orders, even after the death
of their summoner. While they’re incredibly quick
and doggedly persistent, they are, ironically, not
particularly bright. Still, you don’t have to be the
brightest bulb in the pack when you’re literally a
living ball of fire. Oh, and you should probably note
that normal weapons won’t have any effect on these
fiery bastards.

look you in the eye and strong enough to break you
in half? The Rat Brute is a force of raw physical power
and sheer ferocity. The muscles in their jaws alone can
shear through steel. These guys are deranged, too.
They carry mattocks just because they like the feeling
of steel slamming into flesh. On the plus side, you can
always tell when they’re happy because of their bulging
eyes. Just don’t ask what they’re thinking about.
